headline: Board granted tax exemption appeal for five Avesta Housing properties on Cumberland Avenue and Elm and Oxford Streets 3-0.
summary: The Board of Assessment Review continued a hearing on appeals of assessments for properties owned by Avesta Housing Development Corporation at 307 Cumberland Avenue, 220 Oxford Street, 67 Elm Street, 61 Elm Street, and 55 Elm Street. The Board voted 3-0 to grant the appeal, finding the properties qualify for a tax exemption under 36 M.R.S. § 652(1)(A) and (C). The Board also approved the minutes of the August 24, 2026 meeting and authorized its attorney to prepare a written decision within 7 days.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the August 24, 2026 Board of Assessment Review Meeting by a vote of 3-0.
Reopened the public portion of the hearing on the Avesta Housing appeal, approved 3-0.
Closed the public portion of the hearing, approved 3-0.

Granted the appeal of assessments for 307 Cumberland Avenue, 220 Oxford Street, 67 Elm Street, 61 Elm Street, and 55 Elm Street, finding the applicant proved entitlement to the tax exemption under 36 M.R.S. § 652(1)(A) and (C), approved 3-0.
Authorized the Board's Attorney to prepare a written decision to be reviewed and signed within 7 days, approved 3-0.

decision_evidence.quote: Board Chair Larsson moved to approve the minutes of the August 24, 2026 Board of Assessment Review Meeting. Board member Knapp seconded the motion, which was approved by a roll call vote of (3-0).
Board member Lowry moved to re-open the public portion of the hearing at 11:39 a.m. Board Chair Larsson seconded the motion, which was approved by a roll call vote of (3-0).
Board chair Larsson moved to close the public portion of the hearing at 12:42 p.m. Board member Knapp seconded the motion, which was approved by a roll call vote of (3-0).

Attorney Hunter suggested a motion to grant the appeal based on a finding that the applicant has proven entitlement to the tax exemption under 36 M.R.S. § 652(1)(A) and (C) for property of benevolent and charitable institutions, which was moved by Board chair Larsson. Board member Lowry seconded the motion, which was approved by a roll call vote of (3-0).

Board member Lowry motioned to authorize the Board’s Attorney to prepare a written decision to be reviewed and signed within 10 days. Board chair Larsson amended the motion to 7 days to reflect the applicant’s returned decision timeline. Board member Lowry seconded the motion as amended, which was approved by a roll call vote of (3-0).

plain_text:
Board of Assessment Review 
Monday, September 14, 2026, 11:00 AM 
Meeting Minutes 
 
Eric Larsson, Chair 
Dale Knapp 
Lee Lowry 
 
The meeting convened at 11:03 a.m. on September 14, 2026 via Zoom. 
 
Attendees: Board members Eric Larsson, Chair, Dale Knapp, Lee Lowry, Attorney Jonathan 
Hunter representing the board, City Assessor Elisa Marr, Assistant City Assessor Matthew 
Caton, Attorney Michael Goldman representing the city, Attorney Henry Barkley representing 
the taxpayer, Andrew Altmaier and Patrick Hess representing the taxpayer, and board assistant 
Annie James. 
Board attendance was taken by roll call. One member of the public, David Silk, was present. 
 
Approve the Minutes of the August 24, 2026 Board of Assessment Review Meeting 
 
Board Chair Larsson moved to approve the minutes of the August 24, 2026 Board of Assessment 
Review Meeting. Board member Knapp seconded the motion, which was approved by a roll call 
vote of (3-0). The following individuals spoke: Eric Larsson, Attorney Hunter, Attorney Barkley. 
 
Continuation of Appeal of Assessments re: 307 Cumberland Avenue, CBL 033 N018001; 
220 Oxford Street, CBL 033 N003001; 67 Elm Street, CBL 033 N001001; 61 Elm Street, 
CBL 033 N004001; and 55 Elm Street, CBL 033 N006001; Owner Avesta Housing 
Development Corporation 
 
Board Chair Larsson opened the continuation of the appeal of the assessments from Avesta 
Housing Development Corporation. Attorney Hunter provided a summary of the arguments to 
the Board, and shared his screen to display 36 M.R.S. § 652 for the Board to review. The 
following individuals spoke: Eric Larsson, Dale Knapp, Attorney Hunter, Lee Lowry, Annie 
James. 
 
Board member Lowry moved to re-open the public portion of the hearing at 11:39 a.m. Board 
Chair Larsson seconded the motion, which was approved by a roll call vote of (3-0). 
 
The following individuals spoke during the public portion of the hearing: Patrick Hess, Attorney
Goldman, Attorney Barkley. 
 
The Board discussed the factual findings of the appeal. The following individuals spoke: 
Attorney Hunter, Eric Larsson, Lee Lowry, Dale Knapp. 
 
A break was called at 12:34 p.m. 
 
The meeting reconvened at 12:41 p.m. 
 
Board chair Larsson moved to close the public portion of the hearing at 12:42 p.m. Board 
member Knapp seconded the motion, which was approved by a roll call vote of (3-0). 
 
Attorney Hunter suggested a motion to grant the appeal based on a finding that the applicant has 
proven entitlement to the tax exemption under 36 M.R.S. § 652(1)(A) and (C) for property of 
benevolent and charitable institutions, which was moved by Board chair Larsson. Board member 
Lowry seconded the motion, which was approved by a roll call vote of (3-0). 
 
Board member Lowry motioned to authorize the Board’s Attorney to prepare a written decision 
to be reviewed and signed within 10 days. Board chair Larsson amended the motion to 7 days to 
reflect the applicant’s returned decision timeline. Board member Lowry seconded the motion as 
amended, which was approved by a roll call vote of (3-0). 
 
New Business (If Necessary) 
 
The Board did not discuss any new business. 
 
Adjournment 
 
Board chair Larsson moved and Board member Lowry seconded the motion to adjourn, which 
passed by a roll call vote of (3-0). The meeting concluded at 12:47 p.m.
